metadata.case_name: WONG ROCKY LOK KUN v. WU KWONG SUM

plaintiff.occupation_before: Ground services agent at the Hong Kong International Airport (customer services supervisor)

injuries.description: Major Depressive Disorder Single Episode, Mild
source: Dr Hungs diagnosis was Major Depressive Disorder Single Episode, Mild.

manifestations.description: loss of interest in things he used to enjoy
lack of motivation and low energy throughout the day
poor concentration and attention affecting work performance
difficulty remembering new information and materials in new job

treatments_received: psychiatric assessment by Dr Gabriel Hung (assessments in May 2015, 2016 and early 2017)
therapeutic treatment by Dr Cindy Chiu (specialist in psychiatry)

losses.description: The relationship became more and more distant; later the wife refused to sleep in the same room; the wife filed for divorce in 2015; he had limited access to his daughter and missed her a lot.

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
losses.description: The wife became sexually cold and uninterested; the couple did not have any sexual intercourse ever since their daughter was born.

He quit his job as customer services supervisor in March 2016 and took up a less stressful job as an operations trainee at HACTL; his concentration and attention became poor and this affected his work performance; he found it difficult at times to remember all the new information and materials.
Dr Hungs diagnosis was Major Depressive Disorder Single Episode, Mild.

comparable_cases.injury_description: Failed vasectomy leading to the wife becoming pregnant and giving birth to a child; wife claimed damages for pain and distress and was held entitled.
General practitioner negligently failed to diagnose AT's HIV and to advise testing; BT, his sexual partner, contracted HIV and succeeded in claim against the doctor.

Foster parents alleged psychiatric illness (including severe depression and PTSD) after children in their care were sexually abusive; House of Lords held it was arguable that a duty of care was owed to the parents.
